content:
We have carbon NMR peaks: 135.80, 117.40, 70.50, 54.00, 43.70 ppm. Need to determine number of CH3 groups. Methyl carbons typically appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but can be around 50 ppm for O-CH3 (methoxy) or 20-30 for alkyl. Here we have peaks at 54.00 and 43.70, which could be O-CH3 (around 55) and maybe a carbon attached to heteroatom. Also 70.5 could be a carbon bearing OH (CH2). 117-135 are aromatic/sp2. So likely there is one methoxy (CH3 attached to O) giving ~54 ppm. No other low-field aliphatic methyl. So number of CH3 groups = 1.

But need to be sure: Could 43.70 be a methyl attached to N (N-CH3) also around 40-45. So could be second methyl. However typical N-CH3 appears ~30-40. 43.7 could be N-CH3. So maybe there are two methyl groups: one O-CH3 (54) and one N-CH3 (43.7). Without more info, ambiguous. Could use proton NMR to see number of methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
